clue.text: Town race's runners

parts.note: race in the sense of humankind is man, so race's gives man's
the runners in a race are collectively the field

explanation.surface: A town known for the people who ran in a race held there.
explanation.walkthrough: MANSFIELD is a town in Nottinghamshire, England, and also the start of Jane Austen's Mansfield Park, a theme of this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield is a market town in Nottinghamshire, so it is an example of a town.

clue.text: Notes plug about FT

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: taken here as a mic, the microphone a speaker plugs things into
the Financial Times, speaking of itself, is us

explanation.surface: A short memo plugging the Financial Times.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the paper printing the puzzle, so it refers to itself as US.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is written as notes and played as notes, so notes stand for the art itself.

clue.text: Marking tours on Civic Centre, having no choice

indicators.note: tours means goes round, so the marking word encloses the rest

parts.note: marking means noting or observing
taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of the word civic is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Someone noting tours that set off from the civic centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' signals the enclosure; 'Civic Centre' looks like a building but gives only its middle letter V.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-voting member gets no say in a vote, so they have no choice in the decision.

clue.text: Bohemian popular with drinkers?

definitions.meaning: a bohemian is an unconventional, independent person
a ..., read literally, is gin or whisky given away at no charge, which drinkers would welcome

explanation.surface: A bohemian type who goes down well in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian lives unconventionally, the very idea of an uninhibited, independent soul.

clue.text: Fake from Brussels makes agreeable sound

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, EU
fake means phony

explanation.surface: A forgery from Brussels that makes a pleasant noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse of the clue's order: Brussels' EU first, then PHONY.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphony is harmony of sound, a pleasing quality to the ear.

clue.text: Run down steep hill, bathe hot feet in river

indicators.note: in means the picked letters sit inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: the feet of words are their last letters

explanation.surface: After a run down a steep hill, soak hot feet in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' signals the last letters, read as PLET; 'Run down' looks like part of the jog but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to use up or exhaust a supply, which is to run it down.

clue.text: Many cats purr first then hack

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of purr

parts.note: a hack is a ride on horseback

explanation.surface: A cat purrs before coughing something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' looks like a cough or a cut; it is a horse ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is the collective noun for a group of lions, big cats living together.

clue.text: Graham's miner loses old piece of land

indicators.note: loses means the old letters drop out of the miner's name

parts.note: Ross Poldark, the mine-owning hero of Winston Graham's Cornish novels
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miner in a Graham story gives up an old patch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The novels were made into the BBC series Poldark.
explanation.definitionFit: A park is an enclosed area of ground, so it is a piece of land.

clue.text: Mali's new religion

indicators.note: new means the letters are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: Mali taking up a new faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the faith of Muslims, one of the world's major religions.

clue.text: Set out climbing Ulster mountain, heading off cursed outside

indicators.note: outside means the cursed word wraps round the mountain piece
heading off removes the first letter

parts.note: cursed means hexed, put under a spell

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the pieces upwards, backwards

parts.note: Ulster is Northern Ireland, NI
an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: A climber sets off up a mountain in Northern Ireland, swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns NI ALP into PLAIN; 'heading off' drops the H of HEXED, leaving EXED, which goes 'outside' it. 'cursed' suggests swearing; it means bewitched.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out an argument is to state it clearly, which is to explain it.

clue.text: Detect smells in the ear

indicators.note: in the ear means as it is heard, a word that sounds alike

parts.note: smells as a noun means scents

explanation.surface: Picking up odours by the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense something is to perceive or pick it up, so it means to detect.

clue.text: How leaves may be connected to ridiculous apple price cut

indicators.note: ridiculous means the letters are thrown into absurd disorder
cut docks the final letter

explanation.surface: A ridiculous price for apples, now reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the last E of 'price', leaving PRIC, and 'ridiculous' rearranges APPLE plus PRIC. 'leaves' suggests the apple tree; it means sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets or pages of paper are held together by a bent wire clip.

clue.text: Old women seizing corrupt boss is a bit of a warning sign

definitions.text: a bit of a warning sign

indicators.note: seizing means the old women grip the other piece inside them

parts.note: crones are old women

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters are spoiled into another order

explanation.surface: Elderly women grab a crooked boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' gives the scrambled SSBO; 'seizing' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull and crossbones on poison bottles or pirate flags warns of danger, and the bones are part of it.

clue.text: She's not completely jammed in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means the extracted letters are read backwards
not completely means only part of the word jammed is used

explanation.surface: A woman who is only partly stuck, going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' takes AMME from 'jammed'; 'in reverse' reads it backwards. Emma is also a Jane Austen novel, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a woman's name, so a female person, she, fits.

clue.text: Clear spaghetti from meal, the main portion

parts.note: tea is an evening meal in Britain
the main is an old poetic name for the open sea
a portion is a part

explanation.surface: Spaghetti served as the main portion of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To untangle strands of pasta you separate them gently, pulling them free of each other.

clue.text: Power from a dual-fired electricity terminal

parts.note: bi- is the prefix meaning two or dual
fired means lit, set alight

indicators.note: terminal means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Power supplied by a dual-fuel electricity station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' looks like a power-station term; it takes the final Y of 'electricity'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ability is the capacity or power to do something.

clue.text: A cheer burst out having started books

indicators.note: out means the burst word sits outside the cheer

parts.note: to burst is to pop
a cheer is a cry
the start of the word having is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A cheer erupting once something got under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' is the enclosure signal; 'having started' supplies the opening two letters of having.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are biblical books of doubtful authority left out of many canons.

clue.text: New to green part of Manchester

indicators.note: new means the letters are put in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone new to a park in Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: EGERTON is a district of Greater Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Egerton is a village near Bolton in Greater Manchester, so a district of that area.

clue.text: Addressing lecture

definitions.meaning: a lecture is a scolding, a dressing-down

explanation.surface: Delivering a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe reprimand given face to face is a dressing-down or reprimand, also called a lecture.

clue.text: Gaff caught by two endless congas in progress

indicators.note: caught by means the setter is held inside the doubled piece
two means the dance is taken twice
endless takes off both ends

parts.note: the conga is a line dance; two of them are congas
Gaff is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter gets caught up in a couple of conga lines that never end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips CONGA to ONG; 'two' doubles it; 'caught by' puts I, the setter, inside ONGONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ongoing is continuing, still under way.

clue.text: Elderly man briefly hides dark side

indicators.note: hides means the man's name encloses the dark side

parts.note: Greg is the short form of the man's name Gregory
in Chinese philosophy yin is the dark, passive side

explanation.surface: An old man shields his shadowy side.
explanation.definitionFit: Going grey-haired is a sign of age, so greying people are getting on in years.

clue.text: Took stock of red light

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a light

explanation.surface: An inventory check done under red light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took stock' suggests inventory; here stock means livestock, stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustlers steal cattle, so to have taken livestock illegally is to have rustled.

clue.text: Bedrooms essentially make larger place for visitors to crash, allegedly

definitions.text: place for visitors to crash, allegedly

indicators.note: essentially takes the heart of the word, its middle letters

parts.note: to swell is to make or grow larger

explanation.surface: Extending bedrooms so guests have somewhere to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' looks like sleeping over; it means a supposed UFO crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Roswell, New Mexico, is where a flying saucer is said to have crash-landed in 1947.

clue.text: Rough sport ends in damage

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: ends picks the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A rough game ends with injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude can mean crude or roughly made, as in a rude shelter.

clue.text: Level of noise overwhelms little nerd

indicators.note: overwhelms means the noise unit swamps and encloses the other piece

parts.note: dB is the decibel, a measure of sound level
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A small geek drowned out by noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeb is slang for a boring, socially awkward person, close to a geek.

clue.text: U person is a bad influence

indicators.note: bad means the letters are in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A posh person who leads others astray.
explanation.walkthrough: U is British slang for upper-class. Persuasion is also a Jane Austen novel, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Persuasion is the act of influencing someone's beliefs or actions.

clue.text: One Direction exposed by minor third

indicators.note: exposed by means the letters are revealed within the phrase

explanation.surface: The boy band One Direction caught out by a musical interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One Direction' looks like the boy band; it means a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: North is a compass point, one of the four cardinal bearings.

clue.text: Purchase skirts son is pressing

indicators.note: skirts means the purchase word goes round the son

parts.note: to purchase is to buy

explanation.surface: Buying skirts while the son is ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone busy pressing on is occupied and active, hard at work.

clue.text: Before acting, dame chose extreme intolerance

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
Dame Judi Dench is a famous acting dame

indicators.note: extreme takes the outermost letters

explanation.surface: An actress chose bigotry before her acting career.
explanation.walkthrough: Pride and Prejudice is a Jane Austen novel, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice is a preconceived bias, an unfair intolerance of others.

clue.text: Out of range of fire

indicators.note: out of means the letters come out of their order

explanation.surface: Something beyond the range of gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like gunfire; it means passion or rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire is fierce passion or temper, a synonym for rage.

clue.text: A black governor of Westminster, perhaps

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A black man who governs Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: Northanger Abbey, with 23-down, is a Jane Austen novel, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Westminster Abbey is a famous London church, an example of the class.

clue.text: Source of a glint displayed by those looking old to others

indicators.note: displayed by means the letters are shown inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A sparkle seen by those who look old to others.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold filling or cap in the mouth flashes when someone smiles.
